fact: Under `set -euo pipefail` a bare assignment `x="$(f)"` aborts the whole script when f returns non-zero; the errexit exemption only applies inside if/while/&&/||. A library function that gained a `return 1` crashed every blind-audit run whose allowlist override refused all lanes (P2-36).
recommendation: When a sourced function can return non-zero, capture it at the call site: `x="$(f)" || x=""` (or branch on rc), and add a caller test under set -e.

fact: bash reads a script incrementally, so editing scripts/adversarial-review.sh while any process runs it corrupts that run; review runs that use the driver on its own diff must use a frozen copy.
recommendation: Run reviews of the driver from a git-show snapshot (chmod +x) and make all driver edits in one go before running suites that execute it.

fact: A test that "cleans up" a shared machine-wide file (~/.zuvo/adversarial.log) by trimming to a pre-run line count deletes concurrent writers' rows, and a failed count read as 0 empties the file (GNU head -n 0).
recommendation: Never rewrite shared state in tests; count rows read-only and leave them, or sandbox the path via ZUVO_HOME.

fact: A background job inherits ignored signals, and bash can neither trap nor receive a signal that was ignored when it started, so signal-test cases go red reproducibly. Two different sources: any `&` in a non-interactive shell (job control off) starts the job with SIGINT and SIGQUIT set to SIG_IGN (POSIX), but leaves SIGHUP alone; `nohup` is what sets SIGHUP to SIG_IGN. Probe: `perl -e 'print $SIG{INT}'` prints IGNORE under a plain `&`, and $SIG{HUP} prints IGNORE only under nohup.
recommendation: Start signal-test cases through a perl wrapper that resets the disposition to SIG_DFL before exec (`perl -e '$SIG{INT}=$SIG{HUP}="DEFAULT"; exec @ARGV'`); a red signal case from a detached or nohup'd suite is the launcher, not the code, until it reproduces in a foreground run.

fact: Homebrew bash 5.3 in an `env -i` shell with no locale variable can SIGSEGV (status 139) in forked subshells inside libintl_setlocale -> CoreFoundation; /bin/bash 3.2 (no libintl) does not. LC_CTYPE alone does not prevent it: it names one category, and libintl still asks CoreFoundation for the others.
recommendation: Name the C locale (export LANG=C) when LC_ALL and LANG are both unset or empty. scripts/lib/model-subprocess.sh does this at source time, so it covers the scripts that source it first (the adversarial driver, the router, the preflight and model-run directly; install.sh and the four builds through reviewer-lanes.sh); a new entry point that runs bash before sourcing it needs its own guard. Check ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/bash-*.ips before blaming code for a status 139.

fact: AP13 in shared/includes/gate-registry.md and test-audit-batch-prompt.md reads 'zero expect() calls'; a cross-vendor auditor applies it literally to bash/pytest suites and marks every file AUTO TIER-D without scoring Q1-Q25, although the suites assert through check/equal helpers that drive a non-zero exit.
recommendation: Fixed 2026-10-04: AP13 (gate-registry.md and the batch prompt's pre-scan) now counts the file's own runner's assertions (expect/assert*, pytest, unittest, bats status checks, shell checks that fail the run). Tiers recorded for bash/pytest/bats files before that date were never scored; re-audit them instead of reusing them.

fact: adversarial-review.sh chunks large stdin at 'diff --git' boundaries; a `diff -u` patch (no such headers) is treated as one file and truncated at 30k (EXIT 4), and a single file diff over 30k is truncated even when other files chunk cleanly.
recommendation: Feed `git diff` output, and pre-split any file diff over ~26k into consecutive parts each carrying its own 'diff --git' header before piping; run large reviews as parallel shards (4x) to keep wall time near an hour.

fact: tf-ablate runs only jest/vitest/pytest/codeception, so bash suites need scripts/mutation-survivor-reprobe.sh per mutant; inside a `while read` loop the rt call consumes the loop's stdin and the loop stops after one mutant, and an rt infrastructure failure would read as KILLED.
recommendation: Redirect the reprobe's stdin from /dev/null, and wrap the test command so a run without the suite's RESULT line exits 127 (ERROR, never KILLED).

fact: tests/adversarial/test-*.sh use start_test/assert_eq/rc_of that only tests/adversarial/run.sh defines; run alone (bash or rt) each prints 'command not found' and exits 127, which reads like a red test.
recommendation: Run them as `bash tests/adversarial/run.sh <name> …` (through rt on the farm); never report a standalone 127 from that directory as a failing test.

fact: ~/.zuvo/test-audit-batch builds its batch prompts from the ZUVO_BASE install root (the installed plugin), not the checkout, so until install.sh runs after a rubric change on main, test-audit scores with the OLD rules — on 2026-10-05 the pre-6a1dbebb AP13 marked every bash suite AUTO TIER-D.
recommendation: When auditing zuvo-plugin itself after a rubric change, run the setup and group calls with ZUVO_BASE=<the checkout> (or run ./scripts/install.sh first) and check batch-N.prompt carries the current rule.

fact: An rt delta mirror can keep files the branch deleted (ryzen-tf kept scripts/claude-home/ after its removal), so a test that asserts a repository path is ABSENT passes on one farm host and fails on another.
recommendation: Assert what the code under test does (what it writes or refuses), not the checkout's layout; treat a red that appears only on one farm host as a mirror question before a code question.
